title: Introduce geo-lock enforcement and RBACv2 delegated-role mapper with KMS provenance adapter
author: Priya Malhotra
description: Context: Customers operating under regional data residency requirements have asked for a safer, auditable enforcement point that prevents requests from being routed to out-of-region KMS or inference pools when a tenant or route is geo-locked. This PR introduces a lightweight enforcement layer (geo-lock enforcer) that evaluates a location claim on incoming requests, validates against a tenant-bound RBACv2 delegated-role mapping, and annotates audit events with KMS provenance. Motivation: Existing residency hooks were dispersed across routing and KMS allocators which made audits hard to reason about and increased the blast radius for misconfiguration. This change centralizes validation and provenance annotations so policy owners and auditors can trace why a request was allowed or rejected. Changes included: - pkg/policy/geo_enforcer.go: new enforcement module that validates request claims (region, geozone, tenant-assertion) against configured residency policies and RBAC role delegations. - pkg/rbac/delegation_mapper.go: RBACv2 helper that maps incoming operator/service claims to effective delegated roles with expiry and scope checks. - pkg/kms/provenance_adapter.go: wraps KMS allocator calls to emit signed provenance headers (kms-origin-prove) for successful key selections. - api/middleware/auth_geo.go: request middleware that wires enforcement into the API ingress path and short-circuits requests that fail geo-lock checks before model selection. - docs/compliance/geo-locking.md: new guide for compliance and SRE runbooks explaining expected audit fields and how to configure tenant-scoped policies. - helm/redwood/templates/config-enforcer.yaml: helm values and default config for the enforcer and delegation mapper. - tests/integration/geo_lock_e2e_test.go and tests/unit/*: tests covering positive/negative cases, expiry of delegated roles, and audit enrichment formats. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flagged behind runtime.enforcers.geo_lock (default off). 2) Canary on infra stage with subset of tenants pinned to geozone eu-west-1. 3) Monitor audit log volume and audit.provenance.kms-origin metrics for two weeks. 4) Gradual enable in production with weekly checks from compliance. Backwards compatibility: No breaking API behavior when flag is off. When on, requests missing a tenant claim will be rejected by default (documented in runbook). Tests: Added E2E test that simulates operators with delegated-role tokens to ensure enforcement allows valid delegated operations while rejecting cross-region key requests. Security review: Token expiry and delegation TTLs are enforced; mapping logic rejects wildcard delegation unless explicitly allowed per-tenant in Helm values. Performance: Enforcer caches delegation mappings for 5 minutes with invalidation on policy refresh; observed median p50 +0.6ms in a small bench. CI: full unit + integration suite passed; lint warnings fixed. Checklist: - [x] Implementation with unit tests - [x] Integration E2E - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Feature flag and helm values - [x] Security review notes and threat model summary - [x] Telemetry (audit.kms_provenance, enforcer.decisions) Related work: referenced ENG-2547 for the centralized residency model and SEC-89 for KMS provenance requirements. Links: linear/ENG-2547, security/SEC-89. Merge: squash and merge to main after reviewers approved.
